behavioral_effects: None stated. An empty list is a claim that nothing observably changes.
compatibility_impact: Backend API responses gain security headers; the admin UI and docs pages are excluded so their asset loading is untouched. The file-preview iframe contract is unchanged (SAMEORIGIN framing). One pre-existing defect observed while verifying, not fixed here: uploading text/html through the Next proxy fails with 400 because the proxy's formData round-trip appends charset=utf-8 and the backend allowlist matches exact strings - HTML upload currently only works against the backend directly.
reason: Security finding: SecurityHeadersMiddleware exists but is not installed in main.py, and SECURITY.md claims HSTS is set in production middleware while the middleware sets no HSTS - documentation and implementation disagree and backend responses carry no security headers
rollback: git revert removes the middleware installation, the HSTS header, the config exclusion, and the SECURITY.md alignment; reverting reopens both the missing-headers finding and the config-clobbers-sandbox hole.
security_impact: Backend responses now actually carry security headers: SecurityHeadersMiddleware is installed outermost in main.py (CSP default-src self, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy; docs and /admin excluded; per-route opt-downs preserved via setdefault) and sets Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000 includeSubDomains when ENVIRONMENT=production, making the SECURITY.md HSTS claim true. Session also closed a hole that silently defeated the previous session's fix: the next.config.ts header rule for /api/files replaced the handler's sandbox CSP, so /api/files is now excluded from the config catch-all and the handler alone owns file-response headers; JSON error paths on the file routes set an explicit strict header set. Live-verified end to end on a local dev server: uploaded text/html is served with 'sandbox; frame-ancestors self' through the proxy, and non-file paths keep the global headers.
summary: Install the backend security headers middleware and make SECURITY.md match it
